diagram_math_checks.justification: Example lines 32–38 define C_R,C_epsilon^-:[0,2pi] to C and sigma_1,sigma_2:[0,1] to C. The sketch chooses representative radii 0.85<2.4 solely for this same concentric geometry; it does not change arbitrary 0<epsilon<R.

C_R(t)=R exp(it) is counterclockwise: the rendered outer arc increases angle from 120 to 160 degrees. C_epsilon^-(t)=epsilon exp(-it) is clockwise: the inner arrow decreases angle from 155 to 105 degrees. These are k=1 and k=-1 in local thm-winding-number-circle-traversed-k-times, Statement and proof 1.1.

The affine definitions give sigma_1:epsilon to R and sigma_2:R to epsilon (Verification 1.1–1.2). Arrows are placed on distinct portions of the same positive-real segment, pointing right and left. The figure does not falsely separate their traces. Both coefficients are 1, so def-complex-chain-and-cycle Definition retains the segment in the trace despite integral cancellation.

Verification 2.1 and def-complex-chain-and-cycle boundary formula give +1 at R,-1 at epsilon for sigma_1 and the opposite for sigma_2; each circle is closed. The picture has exactly the shared two radial endpoints and two full closed circles, consistent with partial Gamma=0.

Verification 3.1 gives n=1+(-1)=0 inside epsilon, 1+0=1 in the annulus off the radial segment, and 0+0=0 outside R. The three displayed labels are located in those open regions. The figure caption z notin Gamma* and Remarks explicitly exclude all circle and segment trace points, as required by def-integration-and-index-of-complex-chain Definition/Remarks.
The entire pre-existing Verification is byte-preserved; it establishes the cycle, trace, cancellation and index values without the new final Remarks illustration.
